### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Usher syndrome type 2A  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.792)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:12601)

**Proposed mechanism:** USH2A (HGNC:12601) —DISRUPTS→ Usherin protein function in photoreceptor and hair cell integrity (GO:0005887); Usherin protein function in photoreceptor and hair cell integrity (GO:0005887) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000501); Usherin protein function in photoreceptor and hair cell integrity (GO:0005887) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing impairment (HP:0000365). Loss-of-function mutations in the USH2A gene disrupt the function of the Usherin protein, which is critical for maintaining the structural integrity of photoreceptor cells in the retina and hair cells in the inner ear. This disruption leads to progressive retinal degeneration and hearing impairment, manifesting as Usher syndrome type 2A and the other related disorder.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in USH2A that lead to a gain-of-function mechanism or variants in distinct genes that cause both phenotypes. _(variant: gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01 for a pathogenic variant in USH2A)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the downstream consequences of USH2A dysfunction, such as photoreceptor and hair cell maintenance, could offer therapeutic avenues for both conditions.

#### 2. Usher syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.782)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:12601)

**Proposed mechanism:** USH2A (HGNC:12601) —DISRUPTS→ Photoreceptor outer segment development and maintenance (GO:0007455); USH2A (HGNC:12601) —DISRUPTS→ Inner ear development and function (GO:0007409); Photoreceptor outer segment development and maintenance (GO:0007455) —LEADS_TO→ Retinitis pigmentosa (HP:0000501); Inner ear development and function (GO:0007409) —LEADS_TO→ Hearing impairment (HP:0000365). **How to falsify it:** The identification of a pathogenic variant in USH2A that causes a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in one disease while causing a loss-of-function in the other would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, finding that the primary defect in one of the diseases originates from a completely independent pathway not involving USH2A would also falsify this direct link. _(variant: Presence of a common pathogenic loss-of-function variant (e.g., allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD) in USH2A that is not associated with either Bardet-Biedl syndrome or Usher syndrome.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in USH2A offers a potential therapeutic target for both Bardet-Biedl syndrome and Usher syndrome, particularly for gene replacement or gene editing strategies aimed at restoring USH2A function in affected tissues.
